cruxes.title: CAV identity substrate
cruxes.question: On which blockchain identity standard should a connected or autonomous vehicle's DID be anchored?
cruxes.claim: Minimal-state standards are an order of magnitude cheaper to create an identity on; the hybrid sits on the cost/capability frontier at creation and over a vehicle's lifetime.
gaps: After the 2026-10 fixes ERC-735 is the heaviest create (veracity has a deployment price); chapters 5 and 6 need the sentence.
The harness analysis (#36) finds CVIN-Combined dominated by ERC-4337 on six criteria; H5's wording must reconcile with it.
cruxes.examiner: Is "cheaper" robust to the operation definition, and does the frontier survive the harness's six criteria?

cruxes.question: Does blockchain-rooted identity verification fit the V2V safety-message budget?

cruxes.title: Infrastructure messaging (V2I and infrastructure-to-infrastructure)
cruxes.question: Does the same identity layer secure roadside-unit and infrastructure messages (SPaT/MAP, RSU-to-RSU, RSU-to-traffic-management)?
cruxes.claim: An RSU is a DID with a road-authority issuer; signed SPaT reuses the BSM path; revocation of a compromised RSU key is observed within a bounded number of messages.
gaps: No implementation and no measurement exist; design note written 2026-10-09, code waits for audit.
cruxes.examiner: Your title says connected vehicles; where is the infrastructure?

cruxes.title: Revocation freshness
cruxes.question: How quickly does a verifier stop trusting a revoked vehicle key, and at what latency cost?
cruxes.claim: A cached verifier honours a revoked key for at most k-1 further messages; the k that meets the neighbour-saturation target depends on the host and on the refresh mode.
gaps: Choose the k the thesis defends (review-2 decisions 10 and 14).
cruxes.examiner: Is k-1 messages of revocation staleness at 10 Hz acceptable for a safety system?

cruxes.title: MOBI VID lifecycle
cruxes.question: Is the MOBI VID birth certificate and lifecycle realisable across substrates?
cruxes.claim: Birth and lifecycle are native on all five backends; multi-party attestation on three; the profile is MOBI-VID-inspired, checked against the public texts.
gaps: Few of the VID I MUSTs are met and the birth certificate lacks mandatory fields (checklist §1; SC-17, SC-18 pending).
cruxes.examiner: Why call it MOBI if most normative requirements are unmet?

cruxes.title: Privacy and linkability
cruxes.question: What does pseudonymity cost on a public identity registry, and is it effective?
cruxes.claim: A delegate pool is fully linkable by one log query; per-pseudonym DIDs are unlinkable only while attribute-free or relayed.
gaps: Radio, timing and position linkability are future work (SC-02).
cruxes.examiner: Is a public chain compatible with V2X pseudonymity at all?

cruxes.question: What does implemented-but-uncompared surface cost in correctness and security?

gaps: The chapter-6 section is a draft.
